title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: Why do we keep the smallest item in the heap when we’re looking for the kth largest?
teacher_message:
```text
k = 3
nums processed: [4, 12, 7, 9]
heap after processing: [7, 9, 12]
root/minimum: 7
```

The heap keeps the k largest values seen so far. Among these three retained values, 7 is the smallest, with two values larger than it, so 7 is the 3rd-largest. A min-heap places this boundary value at its root, so `heap[0]` identifies the kth-largest candidate.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Contrast why the minimum of the retained k values identifies the kth-largest value.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner asks for an explanation but does not independently state the top-k retention or kth-root relationship.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: So whenever a new number is smaller than the root, I replace the root with it?
teacher_message:
```text
k = 3
nums = [4, 12, 7, 9]
heap after processing nums: [7, 9, 12]

new value = 5
heap after insertion: [5, 7, 12, 9]
remove minimum: 5
heap after correction: [7, 9, 12]

new value = 10
heap after insertion: [7, 9, 12, 10]
remove minimum: 7
heap after correction: [9, 10, 12]
```

No. A smaller new value is not among the k largest values, so inserting it makes it the minimum and it is removed. The root changes only when the new value belongs among the retained k values; then the old minimum is removed. Thus the root remains the boundary between retained and discarded values.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Debug whether replacing the root with a smaller value preserves the kth-root meaning.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner proposes replacing the root with a smaller new number, but does not demonstrate that the root is the minimum among the retained top-k values.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: So I only replace the root when the new number is bigger than it, like 10 replacing 7?
teacher_message:
```text
nums in processing order: [4, 12, 7, 9, 10]
k = 3
heap before 10: [7, 9, 12]
new value: 10
heap after insertion: [7, 9, 12, 10]
remove minimum (old root): 7
heap after correction: [9, 10, 12]
```

Yes—with one precision: when `heap` already has `k` values, a new value larger than `heap[0]` can enter the retained values, so the old root is removed. If it is smaller, it gets removed after insertion. The rule is: insert into `heap`; when its size exceeds `k`, remove the minimum. The remaining root is the kth-largest boundary.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Distinguish when a larger incoming value can change the root while preserving the top-k invariant.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner suggests the correct direction but asks for confirmation and does not independently state why the root represents the kth-largest value.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: Why do we insert it first and then remove the minimum instead of comparing it directly with the root?
teacher_message:
```text
nums in processing order: [4, 12, 7, 9, 10]

heap before current value: [7, 9, 12]
current value: 10
after insertion: [7, 9, 12, 10]
remove minimum: 7
heap after correction: [9, 10, 12]
```

Inserting first creates `k + 1` candidates. Removing the minimum then leaves exactly the `k` largest values among them. Here, 7 is removed because 10 belongs in the retained group. If the current value were smaller than 7, it would be the value removed. This keeps the root as the kth-largest boundary.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner is asking why insertion precedes removing the minimum.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question and does not explain how the minimum among the retained values identifies the kth-largest value.

The remaining root is the kth-largest boundary.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: How do we restore the min-heap after replacing the root?
teacher_message:
```text
nums in processing order: [4, 12, 7, 9, 10]

heap before replacement: [7, 9, 12]
current value: 10
heap after replacing root: [10, 9, 12]

```

Start at the root and compare it with its children. If it is larger than the smaller child, swap them and continue downward. Stop when it is no larger than either child or has no child. The restored root is again the minimum of the retained `k` values, so it remains the kth-largest boundary.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: How do I tell which elements are parents and children in the heap array?
teacher_message:
```text
nums in processing order: [2, 7, 10, 11, 12]

heap: [2, 7, 10, 12, 11]

```

Use zero-based positions. A non-root position’s parent is at `floor((position - 1) / 2)`. Its children are at positions `2 × position + 1` and `2 × position + 2`, when those positions exist. The root is `heap[0]`, the minimum of the retained `k` values.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner is asking how array positions map to parent and child relationships.

model_assessment.rationale: The message asks for the heap-array mapping but does not demonstrate the kth-root invariant.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: The heap contains the `k` largest values seen so far, and `heap[0]` is the smallest of them—the kth-largest.
teacher_message:
```text
nums in processing order: [4, 12, 7, 9]
k = 3
heap: [7, 9, 12]
heap[0]: 7
```

That is the invariant for this concept: `heap` retains the `k` largest values seen so far, and `heap[0]` is the minimum among them, so it represents the kth-largest value.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner states both the retained top-k invariant and the root’s kth-largest meaning.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: The heap contains the `k` largest values seen so far, and `heap[0]` is the smallest of them—the kth-largest.
model_assessment.rationale: The message explicitly connects the minimum of the retained k largest values to the kth-largest result.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: So can I just sort the heap and take its first value as the answer?
teacher_message:
```text
k = 3
initial heap: []                 size = 0 <= k
after 4:       heap = [4]        size = 1 <= k
after 12:      heap = [4, 12]     size = 2 <= k
after 7:       heap = [4, 12, 7]  size = 3 <= k
after 9:       insert, then remove minimum
                heap = [7, 9, 12] size = 3 <= k
```

Sorting `heap` is unnecessary. Initialize `heap` empty, insert each value, and remove its minimum only when its size becomes greater than `k`. This keeps the size bound true after every completed update. What is the size of `heap` immediately after initialization when `k = 3`?

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner asks about sorting `heap` but does not describe its initialization or size bound.

model_assessment.rationale: The question does not demonstrate that `heap` is initialized and maintained with no more than `k` values.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: It’s empty, so the size is 0.
teacher_message:
```text
k = 3
heap: []
size(heap): 0
0 <= k: true
```

Correct. Initializing `heap` as empty gives it size 0, which satisfies the bound `size(heap) <= k`. After each insertion, keep the value if the size is at most `k`; if the size becomes larger than `k`, remove the minimum.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner identifies that the initialized `heap` is empty and has size 0.

model_assessment.rationale: The message does not state the required size relationship between `heap` and `k`.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: When the heap reaches exactly size `k`, do I keep all `k` values until the next insertion?
teacher_message:
```text
k = 3
heap before next insertion: [4, 7, 12]
size(heap): 3 <= k  -> keep all 3

after inserting 9:
size(heap): 4 > k   -> remove minimum 4
heap after correction: [7, 9, 12]
size(heap): 3 <= k
```

Yes. When `heap` has exactly `k` values, keep all of them. Only a later insertion can make its size `k + 1`; then remove the minimum so the size returns to at most `k`.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner asks whether all `k` values remain in `heap` when its size is exactly `k`.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question and does not independently demonstrate the size-bound invariant.
